text: Website tracking is set up by adding a single JavaScript snippet or tag to the page head, like a Google Analytics tag
quote: To start tracking events just add following snippet to the `<head>` section of your website:

text: The JavaScript integration is fully compatible with the Segment API and built on the open-source analytics.js library
quote: Jitsu javascript integration is 100% compatible with Segment API.

text: A React integration is provided for event collection
quote: Jitsu javascript integration is 100% compatible with Segment API. In addition to that we have React integration

text: Backends can send events to Jitsu through an HTTP ingestion API
quote: You can use HTTP API to send data to Jitsu. This is useful if you want to send data from your backend.

text: Ingestion API requests are authenticated with an X-Write-Key header
quote: Use `X-Write-Key` header to authenticate requests.

text: Users can add multiple sites or apps to one Jitsu instance
quote: Add your site or app to Jitsu. You can add multiple sites.

text: Functions filter, transform and enrich events before they are sent to destinations
quote: Filter - Exclude data that fails to meet your specified criteria. Transform - Modify data to fit the schema of your destination. Enrich - Add extra information to the event.

text: Functions can be written in TypeScript or JavaScript
quote: Filter, transform, and enrich events with TypeScript functions before they land.

text: Functions have persistent storage that keeps data between calls
quote: [Persistent Storage](/docs/functions/runtime#persistent-storage) - Maintain data between different function calls.

text: Functions can call third-party services over HTTP through a Fetch API
quote: [Fetch API](/docs/functions/runtime#fetch-api) - Perform HTTP requests to third-party services.

text: Functions can query connected data warehouses through a Warehouse API
quote: `ctx.getWarehouse` - warehouse API to query your data warehouses

text: Functions can log messages, and the logs can be viewed later in Live Events
quote: Persistent Storage - Maintain data between different function calls. Logging - Log messages and access them later in Live Events. Fetch API - Perform HTTP requests to third-party services. Warehouse API - Query your data warehouses.

text: A built-in functions editor and debugger runs a function against sample data
quote: Jitsu comes with a functions debugger/editor that allows to run function on a sample data

text: Filtering events in flight, such as bot hits and health checks, keeps them out of downstream billing
quote: Bot hits and health checks that a function drops on every connection never reach the bill, and the Segment calls in your site, apps and backend stay as they are.

text: Users choose which events flow by connecting or not connecting a source to a destination
quote: You can control which events become active by choosing not to connect a source to a destination or by using a Jitsu Function to filter out unwanted events before they are sent.

text: Once a user is identified, previous anonymous cookie-based records for that user are amended automatically
quote: Once the user identity is known, Jitsu automatically amends all previous records associated with this user based on anonymous cookie-based id.

text: Profile Builder creates customer profile records in the warehouse from traits in identify events
quote: Profile Builder generates profiles based on the `traits` object in `identify` events.

text: Custom JavaScript logic for building profiles can use up to a year of user event data
quote: You can also define custom logic for profile generation using a JavaScript function, allowing you to leverage up to a year’s worth of user events data.

text: Events are delivered to the warehouse in under a second, with optional batching
quote: Sub-second speed of data delivery to your warehouse. Optional batching is also supported

text: Delivers to ClickHouse, BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, Postgres, S3, GCS and dozens of SaaS tools, streamed or micro-batched
quote: Delivery to destinations — ClickHouse, BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, Postgres, S3, GCS, and dozens of SaaS tools, streamed or micro-batched depending on what the destination prefers.

text: Jitsu Cloud provisions a managed ClickHouse warehouse, or data can go to your own BigQuery, Snowflake or Redshift
quote: Jitsu creates the warehouse columns from whatever your site, app or backend sends, in ClickHouse, which Jitsu Cloud provisions for you, or in your own BigQuery, Snowflake or Redshift.

text: Tables and columns are created in the warehouse automatically from the incoming data
quote: Jitsu will automatically create tables and columns in your warehouse based on the data you send

text: While the warehouse is in maintenance, data is held in Kafka and delivered once it is back online
quote: Put your data warehouse in a maintenance mode? Jitsu will keep your data in a Kafka and deliver it once the warehouse is back online

text: Data sent more than once is deduplicated automatically
quote: Send same data as many times as you want. Jitsu will deduplicate it for you

text: A generic HTTP destination sends events to Slack, Discord or any endpoint that accepts HTTP requests
quote: Send data to any HTTP endpoint. You can use this destination to send data to Slack, Discord, or any other service that accepts HTTP requests.

text: Apps send each event once to Jitsu, which sits in front of downstream tools
quote: Put Jitsu in front and your apps send each event once.

text: Connector syncs pull data into the warehouse from third-party sources using Airbyte-compatible connectors
quote: Connector syncs — pull data *into* your warehouse from third-party sources (Airbyte-compatible connectors).

text: Connects to more than 300 data sources, including Google Analytics, Stripe and Postgres
quote: offering seamless connections to over 300+ data sources including giants like Google Analytics, Stripe, and Postgres.

text: A Segment webhook destination streams Segment data into Jitsu and on to your database in real time
quote: Tired of waiting 12 hours until your data is loaded to your warehouse? Set up a webhook destination in Segment and send data to Jitsu and get it into your DB in real-time.

text: Jitsu can run as a Segment sidecar through a plugin that copies data, allowing gradual migration without frontend changes
quote: No need to change your frontend code. Just add a plugin that sends copy of your data to Jitsu. In this mode, you'll be able to migrate to Jitsu gradually.

text: A dead-letter queue with a reprocessing worker lets failed events be replayed instead of lost
quote: Dead-letter queue with a reprocessing worker: failed events can be replayed instead of lost.

text: Live Events data (function logs, batch statuses, delivery results, dead-lettered events) can be exported to your monitoring stack in near real time
quote: Everything you can see in Live Events — function logs, warehouse batch statuses, streaming delivery results, and dead-lettered events — can now be exported to your own monitoring stack in near real time.

text: Exported records use OpenTelemetry OTLP over HTTP and work with Datadog, Grafana Cloud, New Relic, Elastic or any OTel Collector
quote: Records are delivered as OpenTelemetry (OTLP) log records over HTTP, so they work with Datadog, Grafana Cloud, New Relic, Elastic, or any OpenTelemetry Collector.

text: Real-time email or Slack alerts fire when connector sync tasks or warehouse batch jobs fail or recover
quote: Now, you’ll receive real-time Email or Slack alerts whenever a Connector Sync task or Data Warehouse Batch job fails or successfully recovers

text: An official MCP server lets AI agents create destinations, wire streams, inspect Live Events and edit Functions
quote: Jitsu runs an MCP server, so AI agents can manage your pipeline directly: create destinations, wire up streams, inspect Live Events, and edit Functions.

text: Interactive MCP clients authenticate with OAuth 2.1 through browser approval and receive a scoped, revocable token
quote: Approve it once and the client gets a scoped, revocable token.

text: In CI and other headless environments, authentication uses a personal API key
quote: In CI and other headless environments the browser flow can't run. There you authenticate with a personal API key instead

text: A public Management API with a full OpenAPI 3.0 reference is available for every instance
quote: A public Management API for every Jitsu instance, with a full OpenAPI 3.0 reference at docs.jitsu.com/api. jitsu-cli — a real command-line interface that does everything the UI does.

text: The HTTP API manages workspaces, sites, destinations, connections, syncs and functions
quote: Jitsu exposes an HTTP API for managing workspaces, sites, destinations, connections, syncs and functions.

text: jitsu-cli is an official CLI that manages workspace configuration objects such as destinations, streams and connections
quote: `jitsu-cli` is the command-line interface for Jitsu. It manages workspace configuration objects (destinations, streams, connections, …) and runs the Functions dev workflow.

text: jitsu-cli can do everything the UI does
quote: **`jitsu-cli`** — a real command-line interface that does everything the UI does.

text: jitsu-cli scaffolds a TypeScript Functions project with tests and deploys it to the workspace from your own repo
quote: build and deploy them from your own repo with the Jitsu CLI — `jitsu-cli init` scaffolds a TypeScript project with tests, and `jitsu-cli deploy` ships it to your workspace.

text: Named user API tokens with expiration are supported
quote: Audit log (SOC2-oriented) with account-activity alerts, plus named user API tokens with expiration.

text: A SOC2-oriented audit log with account-activity alerts is provided
quote: Audit log (SOC2-oriented) with account-activity alerts, plus named user API tokens with expiration.

text: Jitsu is 100% open source and can be deployed on any on-premise infrastructure
quote: Jitsu is 100% open-source and can be deployed to any on-premise infrastructure.

text: Jitsu can be self-hosted on Kubernetes with Helm
quote: Run Jitsu yourself on Kubernetes with Helm, fully under your control.

text: A development Helm chart deploys the full architecture to Minikube with zero configuration
quote: Development Helm chart: deploy the full architecture to Minikube with zero configuration.

text: Self-hosted functions, Profile Builder and connector syncs run as Kubernetes workloads managed by the Jitsu operator
quote: A feature-complete Jitsu deployment requires a Kubernetes cluster: functions and profile builders run in dedicated function-server deployments managed by the Jitsu operator, and connector syncs run as Kubernetes CronJobs.

text: Deployment options include Jitsu Cloud, Private Cloud and On Prem
quote:
Jitsu Cloud

Jitsu Private Cloud

On Prem

text: Customer data is encrypted at rest with AES-256 and in transit with TLS
quote: All customer data is encrypted at rest with AES-256 and in transit via TLS.

text: Jitsu is SOC 2 compliant
quote: Jitsu is SOC 2 compliant, demonstrating our commitment to maintaining the highest standards of security and data protection.

text: A DPA and Standard Contractual Clauses are available to customers
quote: You can access DPA (Data Processing Agreement) + SCC (Standard Contractual Clause) using this link
